compatibility.version_claim: The package peer range includes the current React 19.1.1 and Three.js 0.186.1 versions.
compatibility.caveat: A declared peer range is not a runtime test. The repository's own development dependencies target Three.js 0.149 and include aliases for Three 0.128 and 0.165. Some public source still uses removed/deprecated color APIs such as `renderer.outputEncoding = THREE.sRGBEncoding` and `texture.encoding = THREE.sRGBEncoding` (for example Gallery.tsx lines 59, 86; glassToggleScene.ts line 354). Current r186 uses `outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace` and `texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace`.
compatibility.minimal_adaptation: Use source as a design/implementation reference, not as a drop-in package. Keep the existing single shared WebGL renderer and scene owner; port only small, needed patterns into the existing React/Three/GSAP/Motion APIs. Translate legacy color-space calls to r186, preserve existing resource/context-loss handling, measure camera bounds at actual viewport ratios, and test reduced-motion plus keyboard/touch behavior.
compatibility.package_install: No installation was attempted or recommended. Whole-package import is unnecessary for selective ideas and would add global CSS/runtime assets; current app already has React, Three, GSAP and Motion.

installed_skill_universe.selection_note: All 144 installed SKILL.md files are the candidate universe. Selected guidance below follows source evidence and the existing web stack; this does not assign or invoke all installed skills.

reference_patterns.title: Frame a mesh/group by camera distance as the viewport changes

source.excerpt: camera.aspect = width / height; ... visibleHeight = max(VIEW_HEIGHT, CONTROL_WIDTH / (WIDTH_SHARE * camera.aspect)) / sizeScale; baseDistance = visibleHeight / (2 * tan(halfFov)); camera.position.z = baseDistance; camera.updateProjectionMatrix();

reference_patterns.applicability: Useful for keeping the Hero's approved subject group or the selected gallery sculpture inside its viewport frame without scaling/reshaping protected artwork. Derive the fit from measured group bounds and camera FOV/aspect; preserve the current camera path and approved B endpoint.
reference_patterns.existing_overlap: The project already owns responsive camera framing in LandingWorldHost/StudioScene and exact scroll camera keys. Treat this as a camera-fit formula reference, not authorization to replace those owners.

reference_patterns.title: Use a group as the transform boundary for a visual collection

source.excerpt: const gallery = new THREE.Group(); scene.add(gallery); ... const panel = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material); gallery.add(panel); ... gallery.rotation.y = elapsed * 0.18; gallery.position.y = sin(elapsed) * 1.5;

reference_patterns.applicability: Group-level transforms let a camera composition or small scene cluster be moved as one authored unit while keeping individual meshes readable. For this project that could inform a measured stage/cluster adjustment, not a continuously rotating carousel or a new renderer.
reference_patterns.existing_overlap: GameGallery already models selectable object groups and focus movement in GalleryCollection.ts. The continuous rotation/bob in this ThreeUI sample is not appropriate to copy; it would fight selection and add idle motion.

reference_patterns.title: Tie a bounded section reveal to ScrollTrigger progress
reference_patterns.applicability: For future authored section transitions, reveal a small related set under one scoped timeline; retain normal document scroll and a complete no-motion state. Translate CDN/global HTML code to local GSAP imports and context cleanup.
reference_patterns.existing_overlap: GSAP/ScrollTrigger already drives this landing's world camera and new story ribbon. Do not layer a second ScrollTrigger on the same camera/DOM property or add generic entrance effects. The example's heading.innerHTML rewrite (lines 232-243) should not be copied; it parses and rewrites markup unsafely.

reference_patterns.title: Keep selection state coherent across focus, pointer, and visual focus

source.excerpt: cards receive click and focus handlers that moveTo(index); pointer coordinates normalize against stage bounds; each card gets aria-current from the same activeIndex.

reference_patterns.applicability: A reference for one selection model driving both visible focus and accessible current state. Its DOM 3D filmstrip could inspire a compact preview composition only if it preserves the existing selected game/art object, keyboard behavior and exact destination.
reference_patterns.existing_overlap: The app already raycasts all eight game sculptures, has keyboard selection and syncs the caption/CTA; do not replace it with a card carousel or copy its perpetual idle phase.

selected_skills.name: ponytail-audit
selected_skills.relevant_instruction: Map real entry/owner paths; report concrete, source-evidenced patterns; do not make vague style recommendations. Read-only audit.

required_reference.instruction: Keep renderer/camera resize and scene-group transforms coherent; dispose geometries, materials, textures and renderer resources.
Frame the full subject group by bounds; fit the visible view, not only camera center. Keep transfer engine-neutral rather than porting Godot/Unity camera APIs.

selected_skills.name: gsap-core
selected_skills.relevant_instruction: Use installed GSAP APIs and current React ownership; do not copy CDN globals.

selected_skills.name: gsap-timeline
selected_skills.relevant_instruction: Build a single authored sequence with explicit timing/labels; keep cleanup tied to its owner.

selected_skills.name: gsap-scrolltrigger
selected_skills.relevant_instruction: Use ScrollTrigger at the timeline/root tween, respect refresh ordering and reduced-motion fallback, avoid stacking triggers on shared targets.

required_reference.instruction: Keep pointer feedback secondary to accessible keyboard/current-state selection and real action reachability.

selected_skills.name: motion
selected_skills.relevant_instruction: Choose Motion for interruptible gesture state if implemented; use existing motion/react without Motion+ components or installation.

nonselected_guidance: The candidate universe includes all installed skills, but this audit found no need to select game-rule/AI/save/network, engine-specific Godot/Unity/native, shader/video-production, or asset-generation skills. ThreeUI's broad catalog includes patterns that are technically interesting but conflict with existing approved art, interaction behavior, or motion constraints; these are explicitly marked not to copy.
